notes:
BM25 (k1 0.9, b 0.6) over the inverted-index reader interface, with two departures, both
measured on bench/queries.json:
  1. a title occurrence counts as titleWeight=2 body occurrences, and the persisted document
     length counts title tokens the same way, so the boost is not cancelled by normalisation;
  2. the score is scaled by (covered idf / coverable idf)^coverage, coverage=1.

Dead end worth not repeating: coverage weighted by the COUNT of matched terms
((matched/known)^2.5) sank the bench "noisy" kind from 1.00 to 0.78 recall@10 — a query of one
signature term plus two corpus-wide common words demoted the documents it was about. Weighting
coverage by idf mass repairs it at every exponent tried (0 to 8), because missing a term nobody
discriminates on then costs almost nothing. `coverable` sums only terms the index has seen, so
an unknown query term cannot punish every document equally.

PARAMS is exported and rank() takes an override argument purely so bench/sweep.mjs can explore
the grid against this exact code — a tuner that reimplements the formula tunes something else.
The grid is flat: k1 0.6-2.0, b 0.2-0.9, titleWeight 1-8 all move mean recall@10 by under one
point on this corpus. Do not read a 0.3% bench win as a real one.

This gate was the one that was NOT real at first: it passed on a scorer with idf removed and on
a scorer with the coverage factor removed, because its assertions were satisfiable by the raw
BM25 sum alone. bench/mutate.mjs found both. The two scenarios were rebuilt to be decided by
the mechanism under test (df 24 vs df 2 for coverage; two partial matches where only idf can
break the tie, with the rare-term document deliberately losing the alphabetical tie-break).
